_meta.title: Articulation — how each English sound is made and FELT
_meta.description: Place x Manner x Voicing for English consonants and vowels, plus a plain 'how a child feels it' cue for the multisensory teaching layer. These are shared facts of articulatory phonetics (not any program's materials).
_meta.source_notes: Articulatory feature scheme: ASHA place/manner/voicing chart; standard phonetics. Multisensory 'feel it' pedagogy validated by Ehri lab (mouth pictures transfer to reading), the visible-mouth study, and the Lindamood/LiPS tradition — cited, NOT reproduced. Voicing test (hand on throat) and manner cues are common field facts.
_meta.note: Consonants keyed by their most common grapheme. Sounds are properties of PHONEMES; a decoder maps grapheme→phoneme first (see phonologicalPatterns.json).

voicingTest: Put a hand on your throat: VOICED sounds buzz (b, z, m), VOICELESS sounds don't (p, s, t).

mannerFeel.stop: a closure then a release — the air is blocked, then pops out (p, t, k, b, d, g)
mannerFeel.nasal: air comes out the NOSE — pinch your nose and the sound stops (m, n, ng)
mannerFeel.fricative: a long, continuous hiss or buzz — the air squeezes through (f, s, sh, th, v, z)
mannerFeel.affricate: a stop THEN a fricative, joined — a tap then a hiss (ch, j)
mannerFeel.liquid: the tongue glides and the air flows around it (l, r)
mannerFeel.glide: the mouth slides toward the next vowel (w, y)

p.feel: lips press together, then pop apart — no throat buzz

t.feel: tongue tip taps behind the top teeth — no buzz

d.feel: tongue tip taps the ridge — throat buzzes

k.feel: back of the tongue lifts to the roof — no buzz

g.feel: back of the tongue lifts — throat buzzes

m.feel: lips closed, humming out the nose

n.feel: tongue tip up, humming out the nose

ng.feel: back of tongue up, humming out the nose

f.feel: top teeth on the bottom lip, air hisses out

s.feel: air hisses over the tongue tip — a snake sound

z.feel: a buzzing hiss — a bee sound

sh.feel: quiet 'shh' air, lips a little round

th.feel: tongue between the teeth, air out (thin)

h.feel: a soft puff from the throat

ch.feel: a tap then a 'shh' — like a sneeze

l.feel: tongue tip up, air slides around the sides

r.feel: tongue pulls back and bunches — nothing touches

w.feel: lips round, then slide to the vowel

y.feel: tongue high, then slides to the vowel

vowels._note: Vowels are 'open' sounds — the voice is on and the air flows freely; you feel them in the JAW (how far it drops), the TONGUE (high/low, front/back), and the LIPS (round or not).

short.feel: a quick, relaxed sound — the jaw and tongue stay loose

long.feel: the vowel 'says its name' — a longer, tenser sound

feelExamples.ee: smile — lips spread wide, tongue high and front (see)
feelExamples.ah: drop the jaw wide open, tongue low (father)
feelExamples.oo: round the lips into a tunnel (moon)
